Data Rebalancing

1. What is Data Rebalancing?
  • When server nodes join or leave the cluster, the partition-to-node mapping changes;
  • Rebalancing is the process of moving partitions between nodes to restore an even distribution;
  • For example, if a 4-node cluster had 256 partitions per node and a 5th node joins, ~51 partitions are moved to the new node;
2. When is Rebalancing Triggered?
  • A server node joins the cluster;
  • A server node leaves the cluster (graceful shutdown or crash);
  • The baseline topology changes (when persistence is enabled);
  • A cache is created or destroyed;
3. Rebalancing Modes
ModeBehavior
SYNC Cache API calls are blocked until rebalancing completes; safest option — all reads see complete data;
ASYNC (default) Rebalancing happens in the background; cache operations work immediately but may miss data that hasn't been rebalanced yet;
NONE No rebalancing occurs; useful if you manage data placement manually; 
CacheConfiguration cfg = new CacheConfiguration("myCache");
cfg.setRebalanceMode(CacheRebalanceMode.ASYNC);
4. Tuning Rebalancing
  • Rebalance batch size — how much data is sent in a single message (default 512 KB): 
    cfg.setRebalanceBatchSize(1024 * 1024); // 1 MB
  • Rebalance throttle — delay between batches to reduce impact on running operations: 
    cfg.setRebalanceThrottle(100); // 100ms between batches
  • Rebalance order — lower values rebalance first; useful for prioritizing critical caches: 
    cfg.setRebalanceOrder(1);
  • Rebalance delay — wait before starting rebalance (to avoid churn from rapid node join/leave): 
    cfg.setRebalanceDelay(5000); // 5 seconds
5. Monitoring Rebalancing
  • Ignite logs rebalancing progress with messages like "Rebalancing started", "Rebalancing complete";
  • Use the CacheMetrics API to check rebalancing state: 
    CacheMetrics metrics = cache.localMetrics();
long keysToRebalance = metrics.getKeysToRebalanceLeft();
